question: Where do the milliseconds of a rebuild actually go? The diagnosis this delivery was handed said the folds; this is the decomposition that answered.

build.note: the BASE, before this delivery. Each term timed on its own over the same sandbox record.

protocol.materializations: each timed over an EMPTY table — the state a rebuild always leaves it in — with the drop/recreate outside the clock
protocol.sandbox: one mkdtemp per regime, destroyed after

per_table_p50_ms.note: the nine other tables, itemized, so the summed row above is checkable

ddl_p50_ms.note: recreating an existing schema is 0.055 ms, so the 0.8 ms of a full rebuild is the DROP

reading: The nine folds are 1.2% of a realistic rebuild and 0.6% of a large one. What costs is reading the chain (30-37%) and writing the rows (~50%, of which the reference index alone is a quarter to a third), plus 0.8 ms of DROP that is flat in the record.
the_reference_index_reads_every_kind: It is one row per appearance and every event has a subject, so no kind is unindexed. The premise that the two facts a channel writes about itself feed nothing is false, and this is where.
the_run_table_reads_every_kind_too: lastFactAt is the latest `at` of any event whose envelope pins it to the run, so the run fold reads the ENVELOPE of every kind whatever its `kind` switch says.
